kjv: shall not always strive with man
mine: will not remain in humankind forever
note: Hebrew yadon is of uncertain meaning; the ancient versions (LXX katameine, Vulgate permanebit) read "remain/abide," while "strive" derives it from din "judge, contend."
Hebrew nephilim is a transliterated term of unclear meaning (perhaps "fallen ones"); "giants" comes from the LXX gigantes and Num 13:33, and states as fact what the text leaves as a name.
Hebrew wayyinnahem means to regret or be sorry; modern "repent" suggests turning from sin, which misleads when said of God.

mine: blameless among the people of his time
note: Hebrew tamim means whole, sound, blameless; "perfect" in 1611 had this sense but now implies sinlessness.
Hebrew tsohar occurs only here; it may mean an opening for light (from tsohorayim "noon") or a roof (cf. Akkadian), and "finish it to a cubit above" fits a roof or an eaves-gap.
